scope: projects/domainspec-v2/formalization current contracts, ontology, method, fixtures, manifest, and documentation

projects/auth-foundation/formalization current ontology projection, case package, FormalClaim v4 predecessor, FormalClaim v5 Lean candidate, InterpretationModel lifecycle, envelope, manifest, validator, and documentation
accepted and historical artifacts inspected for contained drift but not rewritten

findings.conflict: The accepted v3 InterpretationModel says an interpretation change creates a new FormalClaim identity, while FormalClaim v4 correctly excludes InterpretationModel from claim identity.
findings.resolution: A v4 InterpretationModel successor says the change creates a new EvaluationContext identity and does not alter FormalClaim identity. Current case metadata treats v3 as historical semantics and the successor as the active correction candidate.

findings.conflict: Case package v1 makes accepted InterpretationModel a prerequisite for claim-source readiness and has no separate FormalClaim admission state.
findings.resolution: Case package v2 separates business semantic acceptance, FormalClaim draft or admission, and optional EvaluationContext. V1 remains compatibility history.

findings.conflict: The envelope was called self-contained while copied definitions retained external interpretation references.
findings.resolution: The contract now says definition-complete and records that copied external references are opaque traceability metadata, need no dereference for claim meaning, and cannot expand the claim.

findings.conflict: The base ontology adds a normative decision reason and uses assigned-role, NotRevoked, and shorthand Session(q) rules absent from accepted BusinessMeaning v2.
findings.resolution: An exact-reference semantic alignment overlay preserves base bytes while replacing current consumer semantics from accepted definitions and explicitly deprecating the stale expressions.

findings.conflict: L0 required a complete separately reviewed InterpretationModel even though FormalClaim v4 identity does not consume one.
findings.resolution: L0 now requires accepted meaning, exact definition closure, formal signature, proposition, assumptions, profile, and ceiling; InterpretationModel is optional external EvaluationContext work.

findings.conflict: Critical terms were distributed across ontology nodes and schemas without one scoped three-voice definition authority and deterministic index.
findings.resolution: The candidate package-local registry defines 26 critical terms with normative, operational, plain, contextual, boundary, source, owner, and consumer fields; its index closes every entry explicitly.

findings.conflict: Historical reviews, refresh runs, and FormalClaim v3 record the earlier interpretation-bound lifecycle.
findings.resolution: The artifacts remain immutable predecessor evidence and are excluded from current v4 admission or projection paths.

findings.conflict: Consumers lacked a single named vocabulary for distinguishing exact reference, definition closure, signature, claim ceiling, and admission.
findings.resolution: The critical-term registry makes each identity component and authority boundary explicit and case package v2 represents admission separately from claim existence.

findings.conflict: The domain-context voices still named fol-core as the current Auth canonical source after the exact v5 Lean candidate selected lean-dtt.
findings.resolution: The two non-normative domain-context voices now describe the v5 Lean candidate and preserve v4 fol-core as unadmitted predecessor evidence; normative and plain-language definition voices are unchanged.

claim_ceiling: Candidate drift audit and repair inventory. Seven conflicts have candidate mechanical or semantic containment, one predecessor family remains historical, and one InterpretationModel successor requires owner review and acceptance. This audit grants no profile admission, FormalClaim admission, proof, provider execution, publication, deployment, or production authority.
